statement: Let I_n=Fin n={0,...,n-1}, for any natural n including 0. Matrices are real functions on I_n x I_n; (BC)_{ij}=sum_{k in I_n} B_{ik}C_{kj}, and transpose is ordinary transpose. For fp: FloatingPoint u, r denotes its round field and P its InRange predicate. The constructions below specify rounded list accumulation, range predicates, and relations on a supplied upper-triangular matrix R. The sole target theorem says that if A is symmetric positive definite, 0<=u, (n+1)u<1, and R satisfies both the stated rounded recurrence relation and its range conditions, then its symmetric residual R^T R-A is bounded entrywise by gamma(n+1,u) times entryAbs(R^T) entryAbs(R). The perturbation definition gives exactly this residual. Real arithmetic is used throughout, with total real division (a/0=0). Real.sqrt is the nonnegative square root for nonnegative arguments and 0 for negative arguments. Definition domains carry no additional unstated positivity, nonzero, or range assumptions.

targets.name: Cholesky.cholesky_factorization
targets.statement: For every natural n (including 0), every real matrices A,R indexed by I_n x I_n, every real u, and every fp: FloatingPoint u, assume: A is symmetric, meaning A_{ij}=A_{ji} for all i,j in I_n; A is positive definite, meaning for every nonzero real vector x indexed by I_n, sum_{i,j in I_n} x_i A_{ij} x_j>0; 0<=u; (n+1)u<1; SuccessfulRun fp A R; and NoOverflowUnderflow fp A R. Then there exists a real matrix Delta A indexed by I_n x I_n such that Delta A is symmetric, R^T R=A+Delta A, and for every i,j in I_n, |Delta A_{ij}| <= gamma(n+1,u) (entryAbs(R^T) entryAbs(R))_{ij} = ((n+1)u/(1-(n+1)u)) sum_{k in I_n} |R_{ki}| |R_{kj}|. The run and range assumptions are exactly the relations specified in the construction descriptions, for this same fp,A,R. The equation uniquely identifies Delta A with perturbation(A,R). Thus the theorem is a conditional bound for a supplied matrix satisfying the rounded recurrence; it does not establish existence of such a matrix or compute it. There is no further restriction on n; empty-index assertions use their usual vacuous or empty-sum meanings.

constructions.name: Cholesky.FloatingPoint
constructions.description: For each real u this is a structure with the single constructor Cholesky.FloatingPoint.mk. It stores a function r=round: real -> real, a predicate P=InRange: real -> Prop, and a proof that for every real x, P(x) implies that there exists a real delta with |delta|<=u and r(x)=x(1+delta). The supplied round and InRange projections select these fields. No nonnegativity of u, concrete representable set, particular rounding rule, or behavior outside P is imposed by this structure. This is data with a conditional relative-error property, not an algorithm.

constructions.name: Cholesky.gamma
constructions.description: For every natural m and real u, gamma(m,u)=(m u)/(1-m u), with m cast to a real. It is defined for all inputs using total real division, including division by zero. In the target, m=n+1 and the assumed (n+1)u<1 makes the denominator positive.

constructions.name: Cholesky.entryAbs
constructions.description: For every natural n and real matrix B indexed by I_n x I_n, entryAbs(B)_{ij}=|B_{ij}| for all i,j in I_n. This takes entrywise absolute values.

constructions.name: Cholesky.perturbation
constructions.description: For every natural n and real matrices A,R indexed by I_n x I_n, perturbation(A,R)=R^T R-A. Its (i,j) entry is sum_{k in I_n} R_{ki}R_{kj}-A_{ij}. This is a residual defined without additional hypotheses. The target does not refer to this definition by name, but its equation uniquely forces its existential Delta A to equal this construction.

constructions.name: Cholesky.dotTail
constructions.description: For every real u, fp: FloatingPoint u, real accumulator s and finite list L of real pairs, write T(s,L)=dotTail fp s L. Then T(s,[])=s and T(s,(a,b)::L)=T(r(s+r(a b)),L). Thus it processes pairs in list order, rounding each product and then rounding its addition to the current accumulator. This function has no range hypotheses.

constructions.name: Cholesky.roundedDot
constructions.description: For every real u, fp: FloatingPoint u and finite list L of real pairs, write D(L)=roundedDot fp L. Then D([])=0 and D((a,b)::L)=T(r(a b),L), where T is dotTail. A nonempty list initializes the accumulator with the rounded first product, with no addition to zero; each later product and accumulator addition is separately rounded.

constructions.name: Cholesky.dotTailInRange
constructions.description: For every real u, fp: FloatingPoint u, real s and finite list L of real pairs, write H(s,L)=dotTailInRange fp s L. This recursively defined predicate satisfies H(s,[])=True and H(s,(a,b)::L) iff P(a b) and P(s+r(a b)) and H(r(s+r(a b)),L). It records range membership of each exact product and each sum before rounding along the actual rounded accumulators in dotTail. It is a predicate, not a numerical routine.

constructions.name: Cholesky.dotInRange
constructions.description: For every real u, fp: FloatingPoint u and finite list L of real pairs, write G(L)=dotInRange fp L. Then G([])=True, and G((a,b)::L) iff P(a b) and H(r(a b),L), with H=dotTailInRange. It records the range conditions for roundedDot, starting with the first product and then the remaining product/addition steps. It has no initial addition-to-zero condition.

constructions.name: Cholesky.prefixPairs
constructions.description: For every natural n, real matrix R indexed by I_n x I_n, and i,j in I_n, L_{ij}=prefixPairs R i j is the list of pairs (R_{ki},R_{kj}) for k=0,...,i-1 in increasing order. Its length is the natural value of i; it is empty when i=0. List.ofFn runs over Fin(value(i)) and embeds k into Fin n. The supplied auxiliary theorem prefixPairs._proof_1 states that for every n, i in Fin n and k in Fin(value(i)), value(k)<n. This definition applies to all i,j, without requiring i<=j.

constructions.name: Cholesky.updateNumerator
constructions.description: For every natural n, real u, fp: FloatingPoint u, real matrices A,R indexed by I_n x I_n and i,j in I_n, define N_{ij}=updateNumerator fp A R i j. If value(i)=0, N_{ij}=A_{ij}; otherwise N_{ij}=r(A_{ij}-D(L_{ij})), where D=roundedDot fp and L_{ij}=prefixPairs R i j. The first row is returned directly without a rounded subtraction; later rows subtract the rounded prefix dot product and round the result. This function reads the supplied R rather than constructing R.

constructions.name: Cholesky.SuccessfulRun
constructions.description: For every natural n, real u, fp: FloatingPoint u and real matrices A,R indexed by I_n x I_n, this is a proposition with one constructor Cholesky.SuccessfulRun.mk and five proof fields: (1) for all i,j in I_n, j<i implies R_{ij}=0; (2) for all j in I_n, 0<=N_{jj}; (3) for all j in I_n, R_{jj}=r(sqrt(N_{jj})); (4) for all i,j in I_n, i<j implies R_{ii}!=0; (5) for all i,j in I_n, i<j implies R_{ij}=r(N_{ij}/R_{ii}). Here N is updateNumerator for the same fp,A,R. This is a relation certifying upper triangularity and rounded recurrence equations for a supplied R, not an algorithm producing R or an assertion that such an R exists. In particular, the nonzero-diagonal field only applies where there is a later column; it does not require the last diagonal entry to be nonzero.

constructions.name: Cholesky.NoOverflowUnderflow
constructions.description: For every natural n, real u, fp: FloatingPoint u and real matrices A,R indexed by I_n x I_n, this is a proposition with one constructor Cholesky.NoOverflowUnderflow.mk and four proof fields: (1) for all i,j in I_n with i<=j, G(L_{ij}); (2) for all i,j in I_n with i<=j and value(i)!=0, P(A_{ij}-D(L_{ij})); (3) for all i,j in I_n with i<j, P(N_{ij}/R_{ii}); (4) for all j in I_n, P(sqrt(N_{jj})). Here G=dotInRange fp, D=roundedDot fp, L_{ij}=prefixPairs R i j, and N=updateNumerator for the same fp,A,R. These fields record membership of pre-rounding arguments in the arbitrary supplied range predicate P for the upper-triangular recurrence, including the dot-product arguments described recursively. This is a relation on given matrices, not an algorithm or a specification of concrete overflow/underflow thresholds. Nonnegative square-root inputs and nonzero division denominators are not fields of this relation; the corresponding conditions are in SuccessfulRun.

assumptions: The target universally quantifies the implicit natural dimension n, real matrices A,R on Fin n x Fin n, real u, and fp: FloatingPoint u. Matrix indices and every vector in positive definiteness have this same finite index domain.
fp contains the conditional rounding property: for every real x in its supplied InRange predicate, some real delta satisfies |delta|<=u and round(x)=x(1+delta).
The target assumes symmetry and positive definiteness of A, 0<=u, and (n+1)u<1.

The target additionally assumes all five quantified fields of SuccessfulRun fp A R and all four quantified fields of NoOverflowUnderflow fp A R, explicitly rendered in the construction descriptions. These are hypotheses on supplied data, not conclusions inferred from the declarations names.
The individual function definitions only require their stated input domains and fp data; the theorem assumptions are not implicit requirements on those definitions.
